macro.headline: Tech-led pullback but bull regime intact; rotation shifts to Energy and defensives.
macro.story:
The tape is in a controlled pullback rather than a break. SPY sits at 738.18, down 1.23% on the day and 1.67% on the week, below its 50-day but still 6.2% above its 200-day. QQQ has been the drag — off 1.9% on the day, 3.0% over 21 days, RSI at 41.9, MACD negative — while the Dow and Russell are holding above their 50-days. VIX at 18.57 is elevated but not spiking (down 1.1% over 5 days), the 2Y is at 4.31% with RSI 63, the 10Y is at 4.70% pressing 68 RSI, and DXY is quietly firming (RSI 62, above its 50 and 200-day). WTI is up 27% over 21 days at $89.60 and copper is trending, while gold and silver are ticking up short-term but still below both major moving averages.

The tracked conversation leans firmly bullish on the AI capex thesis, and the substance is dominated by Intel's earnings blowout (+11% intraday, revenue and EPS well above consensus, management flagging 'strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years' and supply shortages in wafers, memory and substrates), spillover into memory names (MU, SNDK), continued positioning in AMD, and constructive reads on MSFT, META, GOOGL and NVDA. Against that, a smaller but pointed bearish thread is flagging index-level exhaustion in NDX/QQQ/SPY and — importantly — Oracle 5-year CDS spiking to a record ~203bps, framed as a credit-risk crack inside the AI infrastructure trade. Geopolitical chatter around Iran is present but not the dominant driver today. This is consistent with the price data in one direction and in conflict in another: sentiment's constructive AI-single-name story fits Intel's move, but it does NOT explain why QQQ is the weakest major index and Technology is the worst-scoring sector on the momentum board — the sentiment narrative is lagging the actual rotation out of mega-cap tech into Energy, Utilities and Real Estate.

Under the hood the rotation story is clean: Energy scores 9.8 with RSI 68 and HOT status, Utilities 9.0 HOT, Real Estate and Financials qualifying, while Technology, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary and the Nasdaq 100 are all in bearish/WEAK status. S&P 500 breadth is 21.5% bullish vs 50.9% bearish, 6 of 11 GICS sectors above the 50-day. The washout state machine reads CALM — SPY RSI 44.85 is not below 30, so the validated Engine C bounce combo is NOT active. This is neither a euphoric top nor a washed-out bottom; it is a transitional zone where the index leadership is changing hands.

Forward watch: 10Y yield above 4.70% with RSI 68 is the tightening pressure point — a further push higher pressures long-duration tech. DXY firming while gold/silver stay below their major moving averages keeps the validated dollar-strength → metals-headwind edge in force. The Oracle-CDS thread is a genuine risk flag to track; if it broadens into other AI-infra credits it would break the mega-cap tech bid. Highest-conviction long hunt today is inside the Early-Runway Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing cohort and the Staffing/REIT-Industrial rotators — not the sold-off tech names, however loud the sentiment on them is.

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** Energy is the dominant force this week, but it is a rotation story riding on a sharp back-up in yields and oil, not a broad risk-on impulse. XLE +9.0% on 21d, WTI +27.9%, and 10Y yield +6.4% over the same window all point to the same trade: reflation and geopolitical premium being re-priced simultaneously, while SPY sits essentially flat at +0.6% and below its 50SMA. The tape is choppy at the index level precisely because the leadership underneath is narrow and commodity-linked.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** Regime reads CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL at 6/10 with breadth split (bullish 27.6% vs bearish 41.8% over 5d), and VIX/VIX3M in contango at 18.55/20.54 — no stress bid, but no all-clear either. The curve is repricing hawkish: 2Y at 3.79 with RSI 68.6 and above its upper Bollinger band, 10Y at 4.68 pressing 4.687 resistance. Per our backtest, the 10Y "ceiling" signal DOESN'T HOLD (yields continued rising 53% of the time after prior ceiling calls), so treat this as a trend, not a fade. The DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE — DXY above both 21d and 50d SMA — a durable headwind for Gold (-4.8% vs 50SMA), Silver (-12.4% vs 50SMA), and Copper. TLT at RSI 31.9 is oversold-looking, but TLT mean-reversion DOESN'T HOLD in backtest; it's a downtrend, full stop.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into hard-asset and rate-tolerant cash flows: XLE +9.0%, XLV +6.1%, XLF +3.6%, XLU +2.5% all leading. Materials (-1.1%) and Staples (-0.6%) are lagging despite the "defensive" label, telling you this rotation is about oil and yields, not fear. Industry rotation confirms it: flows into Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and unmapped names — no industries have been kicked out. AI Infrastructure theme is CHASING at day 53 with health 8.0; Precious Metals and Broad Commodity Reflation are both flagged FADING, consistent with the strong-dollar spine.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semiconductors is the obvious "already run" story: HOT 13 months, +258% gain — a record-tying spell with a CEILING flag, and the group is already down -13.1% on 21d despite the trajectory still labeled HOLDING_BULLISH. Manage exits there, not entries. The in-range setups with smart-money flow are more interesting: EOG (Oil & Gas E&P, flow BULLISH, coil 99.7%) is the cleanest expression of the energy spine and E&P is only 5 months into a HOT run — about average length. FRT (REIT - Retail, flow BULLISH, coil 81.6%) sits in a group that is HOT 5 months and only +10% — above typical but nowhere near the +197% max. META (Internet Content, BULLISH, coil 71.0%) and XYZ (Software - Infrastructure, LEAN BULLISH, coil 70.6%) are in industries only 1 month into new hot spells — early innings, below-typical gains so far. Watch retest risk on any of these that pop; 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The 10Y at 4.687 resistance is the tripwire. A clean break above extends the yield trend, keeps DXY firm, and reinforces the energy/financials leadership while pressuring metals and long-duration tech — the current spine holds. A rejection back below 4.51 support flips the story: relief for TLT, pressure off metals, and likely a rotation back toward the semis and growth names that have led YTD. Secondary trigger: WTI holding above 88.66 support keeps XLE and EOG-type setups intact; a break there would gut the reflation leg regardless of what yields do.
